question: A 55-year-old man with long-standing diabetes presents with a fragility fracture. He has chronic renal failure secondary to his diabetes. His serum parathyroid hormone concentration is elevated. You measure his serum concentration of 25(OH)-vitamin D and find it to be normal, but his concentration of 1,25(OH)-vitamin D is decreased. Which of the following represents a correct pairing of his clinical condition and serum calcium level?

options.opa: Primary hyperparathyroidism with elevated serum calcium
options.opb: Primary hyperparathyroidism with low serum calcium
options.opc: Secondary hyperparathyroidism with elevated serum calcium
options.opd: Secondary hyperparathyroidism with low serum calcium
options.ope: Tertiary hyperparathyroidism with low serum calcium
